newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: China's CNPC to negotiate on Kazakh Uzen oilfield.
newsitem.headline: China's CNPC to negotiate on Kazakh Uzen oilfield.

text.p: The China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC) has won exclusive rights to negotiate with Kazakhstan a contract to develop the ex-Soviet state's second largest oilfield, Uzen, the official Khabar news agency said on Friday.

Officials confirmed the news. "Yes, CNPC has won the right for exclusive negotiations with the government, and if within a month we agree on basic conditions, we will start preparing to sign a contract," Birzhan Madiyev, department chief at the finance ministry's state property department, told Reuters.

Madiyev said that, provided the talks are successful, Kazakhstan and CNPC would agree to set up a joint venture on a production sharing basis. He declined to name the sum of investment needed to rehabilitate one of Kazakhstan's oldest fields, but said the minimum investment so far guaranteed by CNPC should be no less than $400 million.
"In general, the talk is about an investment of some one billion dollars," he added.

The tender to attract foreign investment to rehabilitate the decaying Uzen field was announced in autumn last year. U.S. firm Amoco and a consortium of Unocal of the U.S. and Malaysia's state-owned Petronas were other major contestants.
Uzen is located in Western Kazakhstan near the Caspian Sea and has been exploited since 1965. Over 260 million tonnes of oil has been extracted over more than three decades.
Uzen's recoverable reserves now stand at over 200 million tonnes of crude. But output has fallen to 2.7 million tonnes (54,000 barrels per day) from 16 million (320,000 bpd) in its peak year of 1975.
